scope: Independent ecological ledger, shared/isolated body physics and declared body-state transduction; no connected population trainer or new GUI yet.

coverage: Explicit resource allocation, capacity, costs and conservation tolerance
Shared competition, independent external supply and actual coaccess requirements
Resource transfer to offspring and explicit deferral by population/birth budgets
Delayed reproduction boundary and observed parent viability
Body failure never represented as an unobserved Core death
One shared physical clock with actual collisions; independent control cannot influence another habitat
Local inherited sensory/motor identities survive physical instance prefixes
Full solver state, late habitat births, empty populations and reused free-joint bodies
Real offscreen RGB and renderer cleanup; removed slots do not obstruct rangefinders
Interval contact impulse and peak are retained when final contact has ended
Observer labels/order/queries and metadata do not change physical or reference/native Core results
Default on and individual body-state switches, scales, raw zero measurements and port collision checks
Existing standalone world, Lab world revisions and AI authoring integration

limitations: No new full-suite or browser run for this lower-layer phase; frontend code did not change.
The earlier integration round had 39 passes and one fixture failure: it used range instead of the actual rangefinder kind. The corrected fixture is covered in the final run.
The first contact test exposed a final-sample-only observation gap. The implementation now integrates each physical step and the final tests validate actual impacts.
birth_due remains explicitly model_born=false until an actual Runtime coordinator applies inheritance.
Population checkpoints, trainer jobs, graphical ecology settings and report exports are not delivered by this phase.
Resource fields are declared radial simulator fields; no diffusion or occlusion physics is claimed.
Body failure removal is a simulator operation, not a model of corpses or biological death.
Local RGB calibration does not prove cross-GPU determinism; no large-population throughput claim is made.
The Docker application image has not been rebuilt in this phase.
